messages.text:
Build LAZERS’ first durable task runner using XState. A submitted task should execute through an OpenCode worker, undergo verification, and have its outcome and evidence delivered back to the originating Architect. After a crash or restart, it should recover without silently duplicating work or losing recorded progress. The runtime owns execution and state transitions; Architect returns when a decision is needed.

Start with the smallest useful end-to-end increment. Make its real status visible through our existing Tasks panel. The System Flow and Timeline visualizations can follow once the runner produces their underlying data.

messages.text:
The code currently persists immutable `submitted` tasks; neither execution nor XState exists yet. The Tasks panel already has scoped reads and reconnect handling we can extend.

I’d bound this to one worker and one attempt, runtime-run verification, durable outcome delivery, and real panel status—without graphs, automatic repair, Flow, or Timeline. Three choices affect execution safety:

questions.question: After a crash, if OpenCode cannot prove whether a worker or verification command already ran, should this first increment stop for an Architect decision rather than automatically repeat it? Confirmed recorded progress would still recover automatically.

options.label: Stop on uncertainty (Recommended)
options.description: Reconcile known host activity and recorded results; durably block ambiguous side effects with evidence and notify Architect. Never silently repeat them.

options.label: Automatic retry required
options.description: Require automatic continuation even across ambiguous host calls; this expands the increment to host-supported idempotent dispatch or equivalent proof.

questions.question: Where should the first implementation worker make changes?

options.label: Isolated worktree (Recommended)
options.description: Use a dedicated task worktree from the recorded starting commit; return a verified artifact/diff without automatically merging. Uncommitted originating edits are not included.

options.label: Originating workspace
options.description: Work directly in the submitting workspace, serializing execution and preserving existing edits; requires dirty-baseline and concurrent-edit safeguards.

questions.question: When the runner is enabled, which submissions should become executable?

options.label: New submissions only (Recommended)
options.description: Automatically admit new submissions after activation. Keep existing stored tasks historical/non-runnable unless separately authorized; do not execute the old backlog on startup.

options.label: Include existing backlog
options.description: Also admit existing submitted tasks after revalidating prerequisites and authority; old specifications may run.

answers: All open tasks in a session should be a graph right, we should know what we can run, and should let the archetect plan the exeuction strategy, verify state, or escalute to the user if unsure. Tasks are per seesion right, so if you have unfinished tasks in a dead session, the architect should periodically check for orphaned work, if the session isn't archived, the tasks are not orphaned, and we should be watching out for dupes across sessions too right?

messages.text:
Yes—with a distinction: tasks are stored per canonical project and linked to their originating session. That lets us keep session-focused plans while checking for overlap across sessions.

Architect should define dependencies and execution strategy; the runtime should validate readiness, execute, and verify. An idle or disconnected **unarchived** session is not orphaned. A bounded runtime sweep can detect unfinished work whose originating session is archived or missing, then request Architect review rather than repeatedly invoking a model to poll.

For duplicates, retry identity can prevent exact resubmissions; semantic overlap needs Architect judgment, not automatic merging.

questions.question: Should this first increment support only single-task execution plans, or must it already execute multi-task dependency graphs? In either case, include project-wide overlap review, durable session links, and bounded orphan detection; existing tasks must be reviewed/admitted rather than blindly dispatched.

options.label: Single-task plans (Recommended)
options.description: One-node plans and one active worker per project. Architect can inspect existing work and admit a task or leave it blocked; multi-task dependency submission and scheduling follow later.

options.label: Dependency graphs now
options.description: Architect can submit dependencies among multiple tasks; runtime validates cycles/readiness and executes sequentially. Larger first increment, still one worker at a time.

questions.question: For unfinished work whose originating session is archived or missing, what should the first runner do?

options.label: Flag and await reassignment (Recommended)
options.description: Persist an orphan attention reason, retain all progress, and surface it to an active Architect for review. No automatic ownership transfer or replay; an unarchived idle session remains owned.

options.label: Automatically reassign
options.description: Choose another active Architect session and transfer ownership automatically; requires an explicit selection and authorization policy.

Inspected the task schema, SQLite persistence, OpenCode integration reference, Tasks panel, and existing tests. Confirmed execution and XState are not implemented.

**Resolved scope**
- Support dependency graphs now, with Architect defining strategy and runtime owning execution and verification.
- Use isolated worktrees; do not automatically merge into the originating workspace.
- Recover recorded progress, but stop for Architect judgment when repeating a side effect would be uncertain.
- Review existing work before admission; check overlap across sessions.
- Treat idle, unarchived sessions as still owning their tasks.
- Flag archived/missing-session work for explicit reassignment.
- Defer Flow and Timeline.

**Still pending**
- Final executable specification, acceptance checks, and execution limits.
- Task submission and a durable task ID.
- Implementation and verification, including real OpenCode dispatch, crash recovery, outcome delivery, and live Tasks-panel status.

The existing-task listing also returned an output-schema error, so overlap inspection remains unresolved.

Next: finish and submit the bounded runner task using these decisions—without another scope interview. No completion evidence exists yet.

The key here is deterministic tooling to assist the agent with this, we can't trust the agent just figures it out, we give the archetect the tools and messages it needs to assist, and the task panel can have controls and views for auditing this as well by hand.

messages.text: The sqlite database can be used to build relationships for the graph as well, ensure you review the original brief here while deciding how to structure this.

Yes. I’m grounding the structure in the original brief and README contracts: SQLite should store the relationships between versioned plans, tasks, dependency edges, attempts, evidence, and decisions—not just opaque task JSON.

XState will govern runtime transitions; SQLite will preserve their durable records. Graph readiness and recovery checks must run automatically before dispatch, with audit results available to Architect and the Tasks panel. Neither Architect nor panel controls may bypass those checks or directly mark work accepted.
